title: Declare the minimum supported engine version in the client
summary: The client records, in one place, the minimum engine version it supports and exposes it together with its own version in a stable machine-readable form that the installer and the startup check both read, so the requirement is declared once instead of being implied. Producing this version information works with no engine installed.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

result.summary: The client now exposes its own version together with one declared minimum supported engine version in a stable machine-readable report. `forgel_code/__init__.py` keeps the single `MIN_ENGINE_VERSION` declaration and gained `version_report()`, which returns both values from the client's own declaration. `forgel_code/cli.py` recognises the client's `--version` before any command is parsed and answers with either the unchanged human line (`forgel-code <version>`) or, with `--json`, one JSON object carrying `forgel_code_version` and `minimum_engine_version`; the report path touches no engine, no session, no timeout and no network. The human-readable output and every existing command path stay byte-identical. `CHANGELOG.md` records the new report under Unreleased/Added. A new test module `tests/test_version_report.py` checks both values in one report, distinct keys, the client version equalling the built distribution's version, a well-formed minimum, successful production with an unusable engine path and a PATH that resolves nothing, that no engine process is started, the unchanged human output, that only words before the command count as the version request, and that no other product module restates the minimum. The minimum `0.1.0` was chosen as the floor already declared and enforced by the shipped installer and startup check, since the engine has no released version yet. Full gate `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes (378 tests, 0 failures); one earlier full run failed on two pre-existing installer timing tests that pass in isolation and in the following full run. `python -m pytest -q tests/test_version_report.py` passes (11 tests).
assumptions: The minimum supported engine version keeps the value already declared and enforced by the installer (`0.1.0`); the engine has no released version yet, so the value is selected from the existing declaration rather than from a release.

The machine-readable report is the client's own `--version --json` output, one JSON object on stdout with the keys `forgel_code_version` and `minimum_engine_version`, capturable by a script without entering the interactive session.

`--version` is honoured when it appears before any command word, so the client's own version report takes precedence over command parsing; a `--version` appearing after a command word belongs to that command.
The client version in the report is read from the single `__version__` declaration, which the build backend already packs into the distribution metadata.
The startup check from the earlier task (which compares an installed engine against this declaration) is not part of this change; this change only declares the floor and reports it.

review.summary: The change adds `version_report()` to `forgel_code/__init__.py`, returning the package's own `__version__` (the single source read by the build backend and packaging tests) together with the existing single declaration `MIN_ENGINE_VERSION`, and wires `forgel-code --version --json` in `cli.py` before any engine discovery, session, timeout or parser work, so the report is produced with no engine installed and without network access. The human-readable `--version` line is unchanged (`forgel-code <version>`), preserving the previous output, and `version_requested()` only recognises the option before a command name so command arguments are unaffected (e.g. `say --version` stays a phrase). The minimum remains declared exactly once and is still obtained from the declaration by the startup check (`compat.py` imports it), so no second copy is introduced; the new test file exercises the report, the no-engine case, the distribution-version equality and the single declaration. The CHANGELOG entry describes the behaviour accurately and no unrelated or generated files are committed. A minor weak point: `test_the_report_never_runs_the_engine` sets `FAKE_ENGINE_LOG`, which no stub writes, so that particular assertion can never fail; the no-engine test covers the same behaviour by making any engine invocation fail. This is not blocking.

requirements.requirement: FR-1/FR-2: exactly one concrete minimum supported engine version, declared by the client and never inferred at run time.
requirements.note: `MIN_ENGINE_VERSION = "0.1.0"` remains the single literal declaration in `forgel_code/__init__.py`; `version_report()` reads it, nothing infers it from an installed engine or the network.

requirements.requirement: FR-4/AC-1: one stable machine-readable report carrying the client version and the minimum engine version, each unambiguous.
requirements.note: `forgel-code --version --json` prints one JSON object with `forgel_code_version` and `minimum_engine_version`; `report_version()` uses `json.dumps` of `version_report()`.

requirements.requirement: FR-5/FR-6/AC-2: the report succeeds with no engine installed and without contacting the network, depending on no engine call, discovery or configuration.
requirements.note: `main()` handles the version request before `build_parser()`/engine construction; the report path imports only the client's own declaration. Tested with a nonexistent `FORGEL_ENGINE` and an emptied PATH.

requirements.requirement: FR-7/AC-3: the client version in the report is the installed distribution's version.
requirements.note: `_build_backend._read_version()` (unchanged) reads `__version__` from the same module, and `test_the_client_version_is_the_distribution_version` compares the report against that metadata.

requirements.requirement: FR-8/AC-6: the report is machine-consumable and the human-readable version output is unchanged.
requirements.note: `forgel-code --version` still prints `forgel-code <version>` only, asserted by `test_the_human_readable_version_output_is_unchanged`; the JSON form adds no prose.

requirements.requirement: FR-9/AC-5: the minimum appears in exactly one place and consumers obtain it from the declaration.
requirements.note: The report reuses `MIN_ENGINE_VERSION`; the startup check (`compat.py`) and packaging/packaging tests read the same declaration. `tests/test_version_report.py` additionally checks no other product module restates the value.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: the declaration and report belong entirely to the client and need nothing from the engine.
requirements.note: Both live in `forgel_code/__init__.py`; the CLI path executes no engine call.

requirements.requirement: Preserve existing CLI behaviour; the `--version` option is only recognised where it belongs (before a command name).
requirements.note: `version_requested()` stops at the first command name or `--`; `say --version` and `say -- --version` are not treated as version requests, which is covered by tests.

requirements.requirement: AC-7: the client's full automated test suite passes with the change.
requirements.note: QA verdict pass (environment test, e2e, repository test all exit 0).

requirements.requirement: No unrelated, temporary, debug or generated files; only the change set committed.
requirements.note: Attributed files are CHANGELOG.md, forgel_code/__init__.py, forgel_code/cli.py and the new tests/test_version_report.py; worktree clean, no escalated leftovers.

requirements.requirement: No test removals without justification; no weakened tests.
requirements.note: No test removals detected. `test_the_report_never_runs_the_engine` is effectively vacuous (no stub writes `FAKE_ENGINE_LOG`), but the same behaviour is genuinely covered by the missing-engine test, so it is a weak extra check rather than a weakened existing one; not blocking.
